overview: Two categories of genes within an operon system, one coding for a functional protein and the other controlling whether that protein gets made.
genZNote: Structural gene: actually codes for the working protein. Regulatory gene: codes for the protein that decides whether the structural gene gets switched on.

aspects.label: Product Coded For
aspects.valueA: Codes for enzymes or structural proteins that carry out the cell's actual metabolic work.
aspects.valueB: Codes for a regulatory protein, such as a repressor, that controls the expression of structural genes.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: The lacZ, lacY, and lacA genes of the lac operon, coding for enzymes involved in lactose metabolism.
aspects.valueB: The lacI gene, coding for the lac repressor protein.

aspects.label: Role in the Operon
aspects.valueA: The genes actually being turned on or off.
aspects.valueB: The gene controlling whether those structural genes get turned on or off.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The lacI regulatory gene is technically located outside the lac operon itself, even though it directly controls it — a subtle but frequently tested detail.
overlay.memoryTrick: Structural gene = does the work. Regulatory gene = controls whether the work happens.
overlay.commonMisconception: The regulatory gene is not literally part of the operon it controls — in the classic lac operon example, lacI sits just outside the operon it regulates.
